label: alg:bring-brane
title: Bring surface ($\chi = -6$ brane) — substrate constants
html:
Algorithm. Bring surface (\chi = -6 brane) — substrate constants

Algorithm (Bring brane constants). Return the substrate constants of the Bring surface \mathcal{E}_q (Euler characteristic \chi = -6, six torus-knot embeddings, fundamental-group presentation) used by every downstream step.

Input

  • (none — the Bring brane is a fixed geometric object).

Output

  • Tuple (\chi, g, k, \mathrm{Aut}) with \chi = -6, genus g = 4, k = 6 torus-knot embeddings T_{p_i, q_i}, and \mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{E}_q) = S_5.

Algorithm

1. Return χ = -6, g = 4.
2. Return the six embeddings T_{p_i, q_i} for i = 1, …, 6.
3. Return Aut group S_5 (the small simple group acting on
   Bring's coordinate ring).

Correctness conditions

Settled by def:brings-surface: the Bring surface is uniquely characterised (up to isomorphism) by its Euler characteristic and the six-fold S_5-symmetric embedding. No upstream calibration; the values are categorical constants.

Complexity

O(1) — table lookup.

Python API entry point

The Bring constants are produced by the canonical script computations/bring_chiral_fibre_figure.py, which emits the witness JSON consumed by every downstream step. The substrate parameter q_0 and its derived constants live in qou_substrate.constants.

Witness contract

Canonical witness: bring-chiral-fibre-figure.witness.json. Records the six torus-knot embeddings, their chirality, and the S_5 action.

Notes

The Bring brane is not a calibration input — it is a mathematical constant fixed by the rigid-monoidal premise. The choice of \chi = -6 is what gives the substrate its 6-knot decomposition and ultimately the torsion structure that feeds Step 7 (GB filtration).
